Christopher Harborne.description: A Thailand-based businessman who made his money in aviation and jet fuel trading, and was an early investor in Bitcoin and Ethereum. Reform UK's largest single donor.

Ben Delo.description: Co-founder of BitMEX, a cryptocurrency derivatives exchange. Pleaded guilty in the US in 2022 to a Bank Secrecy Act violation over BitMEX's anti-money-laundering controls, and was pardoned by President Trump in 2025.

David Grainger.description: A partner at Medicxi, a life-sciences venture capital firm, investing in health, biotech and longevity research.

Nicholas Candy.description: A property developer who, with his brother Christian, built the luxury Candy & Candy development business (including One Hyde Park in London). Left the Conservative Party in December 2024 to become Reform UK's treasurer.

David Sainsbury.description: Former chairman of Sainsbury's supermarkets (1992–1997) and a Labour government science minister (1998–2006). One of the largest individual political donors in British history, having also given large sums to the Liberal Democrats.

Gary Lubner.description: Former CEO of Belron, the parent company of Autoglass, from 2000 to 2023. Trained as a chartered accountant before an MBA at London Business School.

Jeremy Hosking.description: An investment manager and co-founder of Marathon Asset Management. A major Brexit-era donor (including to Vote Leave), and the founding and principal funder of Laurence Fox's Reclaim Party.

Simon Ruddick.description: A hedge fund financier who co-founded Albourne Partners, a hedge fund advisory firm.

Neale Powell-Cook.description: Owner and CEO of Golden Acre Foods; previously Group Finance Director at the dairy company Lactalis.

Mark Petterson.description: A former BP petroleum engineer who went on to found North Sea Gas Limited and co-found Warwick Energy, a wind power developer.

Bassim Haidar.description: Born in Nigeria to Lebanese parents, he made his fortune modernising communications networks in Nigeria and moved to the UK in 2010. His businesses include property, a Caribbean hotel and a loans company. Previously gave the Conservatives more than £700,000, then pledged £1 million to Reform UK in April 2025.

Suneil Setiya.description: Co-founder of Quadrature Capital, a London trading firm, with Greg Skinner. In 2024 he donated £4 million to Labour via Quadrature, which was widely reported as the largest single gift the party had received.

Greg Skinner.description: Co-founder of Quadrature Capital, a London trading firm, with Suneil Setiya; the two met at G-Research. Quadrature gave Labour £4 million in 2024.

Alasdair Locke.description: Former executive chairman of the Scottish oil services company Abbot Group (until 2009) and chairman of First Property Group. Chairman of the Scottish Conservative Party since November 2024, and an earlier donor to Russell Findlay's leadership campaign.

Michael Hintze.description: Founded the asset manager CQS in 1999. A long-standing Conservative donor and lender, made a life peer (Baron Hintze) in November 2022.

Francesca Perrin.description: One of the three daughters of Lord Sainsbury. Founder and director of the Indigo Trust, a grant-making foundation funding projects in the UK and Africa, and a former adviser in the Prime Minister's Strategy Unit under Tony Blair and Gordon Brown.

Kamal Pankhania.description: Chief Executive of the Westcombe Group, a property development company, including its hotel arm Acre Hotels Collection. His Westcombe Foundation funds disaster relief and infrastructure abroad and works with UK charities.

Isabel Goldsmith.description: Daughter of Sir James Goldsmith and the Bolivian heiress Maria Isabel Patiño, and half-sister of the Conservative politician Zac Goldsmith. Described as an art collector.
